newsitem.title: USA: SOCCER-U.S. AND JAMAICA DRAW IN WORLD CUP QUALIFIER.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-U.S. AND JAMAICA DRAW IN WORLD CUP QUALIFIER.

text.p: The United States and Jamaica drew 0-0 Sunday in a CONCACAF region World Cup qualifying soccer match before 35,246 at the National Stadium.
The match was the first for both nations in the final round of qualification for the 1998 World Cup in France.
Jamaica had the better run of play in the first half, but were unable to finish off two chances that could have changed the outcome against the defensively postured U.S. side.
In the 30th minute, forward Walter Boyd was denied by U.S. and Leicester City goalkeeper Kasey Keller from six meters as a diving Keller snuffed a low shot in a clot of players by the left post.
At 45 minutes, Andrew Williams put Theodore Whitmore through, but Whitmore's shot was cleared off the U.S. goal line by defender Mike Burns.

The Jamaicans had a trio of corner kicks in the dying minutes of the match, but were thwarted by Keller, who parried a Williams corner over the bar and followed by making a diving clearance on a corner by Gregory Messam.
"I'm pleased with the result," U.S. coach Steve Sampson said. "Any game in the qualifying rounds is a make-or-break game, but the onus is really on the home team to win."
The second half was more evenly played.

The Americans' best opportunity came in the 60th minute when Eric Wynalda hit a cross to Brian McBride on the right side. McBride headed back to Wynalda at the left post where his volley was deflected by goalkeeper Warren Barrett.
American Roy Lassiter had a near breakaway at 71 minutes, but was stopped on a lunging tackle by defender Durrent Brown in the middle of the Jamaicans' box.

"I expected more from the U.S.," said Jamaican coach Rene Simoes. "I think we had more control is the first half but they are a team with far more experience. Because of that, I thought they would show more."
The match was played in 32 degree Celsius weather and hampered by winds gusting 40-50 kph, making it difficult for both sides to control the ball on the rock-hard field.
"Considering everything, we played pretty well," said Keller. "We'll take a draw on the road and look to win the games at home. Then we'll be on our way to France."

Jamaica: Warren Barrett, Dean Sewell, Linval Dixon, Durrent Brown (Paul Young, 74), Ian Goodison, Gregory Messam, Peter Cargill, Stephen Malcolm (Onandi Lowe, 46), Theodore Whitmore, Andrew Williams, Walter Boyd.

United States: Kasey Keller, Mike Burns, Alexi Lalas, Thomas Dooley, Jeff Agoos, John Harkes, Claudio Reyna (Mike Sorber, 81), Ernie Stewart, Colby Jones, Eric Wynalda, Brian McBride (Roy Lassiter, 60).
